summary: Private deployment: reverse-proxy path-prefix stripping causes SAML/OIDC tenant assertion mismatch and 403 on login
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403s during SSO login to Redwood Private console. The failure appears immediately after IdP redirect back to the tenant callback URL. Impact: All users from Bluecrest cannot complete SSO for their tenant and are hitting 403 or tenant-default redirects. Environment: Private deployment behind a customer-managed reverse proxy that adds X-Forwarded-Prefix=/platform and rewrites upstream paths.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private deployment with tenant-scoped SSO (SAML or OIDC) and set callback URL to https://console.example.com/t/{tenant}/sso/callback
2) Place a reverse proxy in front that uses path prefixing (e.g., proxy serves /platform/ -> upstream /)
3) Initiate SSO from console, authenticate at IdP, observe redirect back to the tenant callback
4) Observe browser ends up at tenant root or shows 403 instead of completing session bind
logs: 2026-03-10T15:12:08Z identity-proxy ERROR recipient-mismatch: expected 'https://console.example.com/t/bluecrest/sso/callback' but got 'https://console.example.com/platform/t/bluecrest/sso/callback'
2026-03-10T15:12:08Z auth WARN relaystate-lost: RelayState empty after proxy rewrite
2026-03-10T15:12:09Z app INFO session-failure tenant=bluecrest reason='assertion_recipient_mismatch' status=403
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Ava Mitchell): Customer says SSO redirect comes back with a '/platform/' prefix injected by their front proxy. They see 403 and session never created. Asking for recommended proxy config and whether Redwood can accept forwarded-prefix headers.

2026-03-10 - Customer (Bluecrest SSO Admin): Confirmed we added a path-based mount at /platform for other apps; upstream expects original path. We can change proxy but prefer to allow forwarding headers if safe.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Diego Ramos): Reproduced locally with Nginx config that sets X-Forwarded-Prefix. Identity-proxy currently validates assertion Recipient and Audience against configured external URL without considering X-Forwarded-Prefix. Filed a small fix to canonicalize incoming host+prefix handling.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Maya Patel): Risk assessment: allowing arbitrary X-Forwarded-Prefix without a trust boundary can open redirect/audience attacks. Proposed solution: support a configured trusted_prefixes list so proxy-originated prefixes are whitelisted and canonicalized before assertion validation.

2026-03-12 - Support (Ava Mitchell): Shared workaround with customer: update upstream config to preserve original request URL to the identity-proxy (remove prefix rewrite) OR configure proxy to set X-Forwarded-Prefix and allowlist the prefix in our private deployment configuration. Customer to confirm which they prefer.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: header clipping or token truncation (previous similar issues) — but logs show full assertion and explicit recipient mismatch comparing expected vs observed callback URL.

Reproduction: set up local proxy with 'sub_filter' style rewrite adding '/platform' prefix. Identity-proxy logged recipient mismatch. When proxy forwarded X-Forwarded-Prefix='/platform' and we canonicalized using that header, validation passed.
Security review: we must not implicitly trust X-Forwarded-Prefix unless it comes from a trusted reverse proxy (customer-managed). Implement allowlist config for private deployments.

Config surfaces: private control plane needs two new fields: trusted_proxy_cidrs and trusted_prefixes. Also add clear docs and a startup validation to warn if X-Forwarded-* headers are present without trust configured.
root_cause: The customer reverse proxy rewrites inbound paths with a '/platform' prefix while the identity-proxy validated SAML/OIDC assertion recipient against the raw configured external URL. The proxy did not preserve the original path expected by the identity-proxy, causing assertion recipient/audience mismatch and subsequent 403s.
resolution: Workaround provided: update reverse proxy to preserve upstream path (avoid insertion of prefix) OR configure proxy to set X-Forwarded-Prefix and add that prefix to the customer's 'trusted_prefixes' in the private control plane. Engineering change: implement an allowlist for X-Forwarded-Prefix handling in identity-proxy and add startup warnings. Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1783 (under review).
postmortem_actions: Action 1: Add documented guidance to 'private-sso-debugging' runbook about proxies that rewrite paths and the two mitigations (preserve path vs. set trusted prefix).
Action 2: Add configuration knobs in private control plane for trusted_proxy_cidrs and trusted_prefixes (backend/ops work).
Action 3: Ship identity-proxy PR that canonicalizes request URL using allowlisted prefixes and add unit/integration tests for SAML recipient validation.
